source.unit: III.13 connected paragraph run from the inference about uterus/stomach/gall-bladder sharing a duct through the comparison of unequal desire and the stomach drawing from a satisfied liver, printedpp291-295.
source.checked: Bounded complete paragraph run read; not claimed to reproduce the entire longerIII.13 chapter.
source.content: Galen generalizes shared channels to alimentary transfer. Feeding and fasting change which organ draws; purgation is another case. Relative demand can override ordinary strength, illustrated by two people competing for food.

design.whole_passage_relation: Complete source-bound account names the analogical organ examples, preserves the drug comparison, then gives forward and reverse transfer with the same participants and channel and the concluding demand argument.
two_reused_input_cases: Abundant alimentary contents with liver demand: gut-to-liver transfer.
Satisfied liver with empty demanding stomach: reverse transfer through the same channel.
design.rival: Two permanently directed vessels or two different substances flowing one way each.
design.distinct_consequence: Channel identity survives direction reversal; comparison concerns the same roles at different times, not simultaneous opposite flow.
design.falsifier: Fail if completing the reversal requires changing the exact channel noun or inventing a second conduit, or if written simultaneity makes the two source cases concurrent.
design.smallest_step: Write a full two-case proposition sequence, including source analogy and guards; freeze SAME_CHANNEL versus TWO_CHANNELS rivals and check all repeated referents.
